channel.title: Cadillac recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Cadillac Escalade IQ and GMC Hummer EV battery fire risk
item.description: A part inside the big battery pack that powers these electric vehicles may not have been fastened down properly. If it comes loose, it can shift around and damage the battery, and a damaged battery can catch fire. You cannot see or hear this problem from the driver's seat, so there is no warning sign to watch for. Your dealer will replace the entire high-voltage battery pack at no cost to you.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevy and GMC SUVs: wrong front wheel bolts
item.description: Some of these large SUVs left the factory with the wrong bolts installed on the left and right front wheel hubs. Over time those bolts can work loose or bend out of shape, and a bolt can break. Only vehicles built with the 24-inch wheels are affected. If a bolt loosens or breaks while you are driving, you can lose control of the vehicle. A dealer will replace both front wheel hub bolts for free; owner letters went out June 18, 2026.

item.title: GM and Cadillac vehicles missing electronic owner's manual download
item.description: The radio in these vehicles was not set to the right status at the factory, so it never downloaded the electronic owner's manual that is meant to live on the dashboard screen. Nothing mechanical is wrong with the vehicle. The concern is that without the manual, owners may not find instructions for using the vehicle safely — including airbag and seating information — and could be hurt in a crash as a result. A dealer resets the radio so the manual downloads automatically.

item.title: Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and Escalade rear wheels may lock
item.description: These 2022 full-size SUVs with the 10-speed automatic transmission have a part inside the transmission, the control valve, that can fail. If it does, the rear wheels can lock up while you are driving, which can make you lose control or be struck from behind. Dealers will install new transmission control software at no cost. GM mailed owner letters on April 7, 2026, and affected vehicle numbers have been searchable since February 12, 2026.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq backup camera screen may go gray
item.description: The screen that shows the view behind you when you shift into reverse can turn gray with no camera picture at all. Without that view, it is harder to see a child, a pet, or an object behind the vehicle while you are backing up, which raises the chance of a crash. The fix is a software update for the vehicle's cockpit computer. Cadillac can send it to your Lyriq wirelessly, or a dealer can install it. Either way it is free.

item.title: Cadillac Optiq and Equinox EV tire tread can peel off
item.description: Some 2025-2026 Cadillac Optiq and Chevrolet Equinox EV vehicles came with 21-inch Continental all-season tires. On one or more of these tires, the tread — the rubber layer that grips the road — can come partly or completely off the tire. Dealers will look at all four tires and replace any that were built during a specific production week, free of charge. GM mailed owner notification letters on November 19, 2025.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevy, GMC Diesel SUVs May Leak Fuel
item.description: Some of these SUVs with the 6-cylinder diesel engine had their original fuel tank replaced with the wrong one at some point. The incorrect tank can let fuel leak out if the vehicle rolls over in a crash. Leaking fuel near anything hot or sparking can start a fire. A dealer will check which tank is on your vehicle and install the correct one if the wrong tank is found, at no cost.

item.title: Cadillac LYRIQ and VISTIQ Battery Bolts May Be Loose
item.description: The big high-voltage battery that powers these electric Cadillacs is bolted to the floor of the vehicle. On the ones being recalled, some of those bolts may be missing or not tightened enough. A battery that is not held down firmly can be damaged in a crash, and a damaged electric-car battery can catch fire. Dealers will look at the bolts and tighten or replace whatever is needed, free of charge. Owner letters are going out in September 2025.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq driver display may go blank while driving
item.description: The screen in front of the driver can suddenly go dark while you are driving. When it does, you lose the information it shows — your speed, the warning lights that tell you something is wrong with the car, and the backup camera picture when you shift into reverse. Driving without that information makes a crash more likely. GM will fix it with new software for the display's control module, installed either at a dealer or sent to your car over the air.

item.title: Chevrolet, GMC and Cadillac 6.2L V8 engines may fail
item.description: These full-size trucks and SUVs have the 6.2-liter V8 gas engine. Some were built with faulty connecting rods or crankshafts — heavy internal parts that keep the engine turning. Those parts can break, damaging the engine badly enough that it quits. Dealers will inspect your engine and repair or replace it if needed. If it passes inspection, they will switch it to a thicker oil, put on a new oil filter and oil fill cap, and update your owner's manual. All free.

item.title: Cadillac LYRIQ front sway bar bolts can loosen
item.description: The bolts holding a front anti-sway bar bracket to the frame may not have been tightened properly when the car was built. Over time those bolts can work loose and come out, letting the bar or its bracket break free underneath the car. A loose bar can then hit and damage the high-voltage cables or the battery cooling lines. If that happens, the car can shut down while you are driving and lose power.

item.title: Cadillac LYRIQ owner's manual misdescribes rear head restraints
item.description: GM found that the owner's manual for some 2025 Cadillac LYRIQ vehicles describes the rear outside head restraints — the padded headrests above the back seats — incorrectly. Following the wrong pictures and instructions, someone could set those headrests to the wrong position. A headrest that is not adjusted properly does not support a passenger's head the way it should, so someone could be injured more seriously in a crash.

item.title: GM cars may lose electric power steering assist
item.description: Certain Cadillac CTS and ATS models and Chevrolet Camaro and Corvette models may lose their electric power steering assist. When that help goes away, the steering wheel becomes much harder to turn, which is most noticeable when you are driving slowly or parking. You can still steer, but it takes considerably more muscle and can catch you off guard. Dealers will replace the power steering gear assembly at no charge. GM mailed owner notification letters on April 15, 2025.

item.title: Cadillac and Camaro transmission may lock the wheels
item.description: Certain Cadillac CT4, CT5, CT6 and Chevrolet Camaro models with the 10-speed automatic transmission can suffer internal damage inside the transmission. If that happens, the wheels can suddenly lock up, meaning they stop turning while you are driving and you lose control of the car. GM dealers will install new monitoring software in the transmission's computer so the problem can be caught, and the work costs you nothing.

item.title: Cadillac XT4 dashboard may block passenger airbag from deploying
item.description: The passenger airbag sits under the dashboard and is designed to burst through a thin, pre-scored seam in the dash cover when it inflates. On these XT4s, that seam may be missing from the underside of the cover. Without it, the passenger airbag may not open the way it is supposed to in a crash, so a front-seat passenger may not get the protection they should. Dealers replace the upper dashboard cover.

item.title: Chevy, GMC and Cadillac diesels: rear wheels can lock
item.description: A part inside the automatic transmission, called the control valve, can fail on these diesel-powered pickups and large SUVs. If it breaks, the rear wheels can suddenly lock up while you are driving, which can make the vehicle skid or spin. Your dealer will load new transmission computer software free of charge. That software also checks for a bad control valve, and GM has a special coverage program to pay for repairing transmissions found to have one.

item.title: Chevy, GMC and Cadillac trucks miss brake fluid warning
item.description: Your truck or SUV has a computer that watches the brake system. Because of a software problem, that computer may not turn on the dashboard warning light when brake fluid gets low. You could keep driving without knowing anything is wrong, and low fluid can make the brakes work less well. The fix is new software, sent to your vehicle over the air or installed by a dealer.

item.title: Cadillac LYRIQ brakes can lose pressure from ABS
item.description: On these all-wheel-drive electric Cadillacs, the anti-lock braking system can switch on when it should not and let go of the pressure in the brakes. If that happens while you are stopping, you can suddenly lose braking ability. The fix is updated software for the electronic brake control computer. It can come to the car as a wireless over-the-air update, or a dealer can install it. Either way it is free. Owner letters were mailed in September 2024.

item.title: Cadillac XT4 and Chevrolet Malibu came with wrong owner's manual
item.description: Some 2024 Cadillac XT4 and Chevrolet Malibu vehicles were delivered with the wrong owner's manual in the glove box. The manual belongs to a different vehicle, so the information in it about how your car works — including safety details such as child seat anchors — may not be correct. Following wrong instructions could lead you to use the vehicle improperly. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal rule for child restraint anchorage systems. A dealer will hand you the correct manual for free.

item.title: Cadillac XT5 and XT6 dashboard lights may not illuminate
item.description: On these Cadillacs, the indicators on the instrument panel may not light up when you switch on the hazard lights, the high beams or a turn signal. Those small reminders are how you notice the lights are still running, so you could leave a turn signal or your high beams on without realizing it, which confuses other drivers around you. These vehicles do not meet two federal rules. Dealers update the instrument panel software at no charge.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq and Other GM EVs Can Lose Power
item.description: The wires inside the electric motor that drives the rear wheels may not be properly insulated. If two of them touch, the motor can lose power, and the vehicle can stop pulling while you are driving. Because these are electric vehicles, that means no power to the wheels at all. General Motors is fixing it by replacing the entire rear drive unit, the motor package at the back of the vehicle, free of charge at your dealer.

item.title: Cadillac XT5 driver airbag may tear when deploying
item.description: On certain 2024 Cadillac XT5 vehicles, the fabric cushion of the driver's front airbag can tear as it inflates during a crash. If the bag rips, it won't inflate and protect the driver the way it was designed to. You can't tell whether your airbag has this problem by looking at it — it only shows up in a crash. Dealers will replace the whole driver's front airbag module free of charge.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq rear seat belt anchor may be weak
item.description: The metal bracket that holds the rear seat belts to the seat frame may have been welded poorly at the factory. This affects the left rear and middle rear belts. If the weld gives way in a crash, those belts may not hold the person wearing them, and they could be badly hurt. Cadillac says nobody should sit in the left rear or center rear seat until it is fixed. A dealer replaces the rear seat cushion frame.

item.title: Cadillac LYRIQ may not make pedestrian warning sounds
item.description: Some 2023 Cadillac LYRIQ electric vehicles received incorrectly set-up software in the module that controls body electronics. Because of this, the vehicle may not make the warning sounds that alert people nearby that a car is approaching. Electric vehicles run very quietly, so these sounds are what pedestrians rely on to hear you coming — especially in parking lots and on sidewalks. The dealer will reprogram the module so the sounds work again.

item.title: GMC Acadia and Cadillac XT5, XT6 Windshield Bonding Problem
item.description: Windshields are glued to the body with a strong sealant that helps hold the glass in place during a crash. On some of these vehicles the windshield was installed without the proper sealant, so it may not be properly bonded. In a crash the windshield could come loose or detach, and people inside could be hurt worse. The dealer inspects the windshield, applies primer and sealant, and replaces the glass if it is damaged, all free of charge.

item.title: Cadillac Escalade, Tahoe and Yukon rear suspension bolts break
item.description: The bolts that hold the rear suspension arms on your SUV were not heat-treated properly at the factory, so they are weaker than they should be. A weak bolt can snap while you are driving. If one breaks, the rear wheel on that side can shift out of alignment, which can make the vehicle hard to control and lead to a crash. Dealers will replace both rear outer control arm bolts with correct ones at no charge.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq battery connections may cut drive power
item.description: Some 2023 Cadillac Lyriq and 2022 GMC Hummer EV models have connections inside the big high-voltage battery pack that may be out of position or welded wrong. A bad connection there can cut the power that drives the wheels, so the vehicle can lose the power to move while you are driving. Dealers will open up and inspect the battery pack and replace the whole pack if they find a problem. GM mailed owners a separate letter explaining the safety risk.

item.title: GM SUVs may lose power from faulty transmission gear
item.description: The transmission in these Cadillac, Chevrolet and GMC SUVs may have been built with the wrong gear inside. Because of that, the axle shaft on the driver's side can come apart from the transmission. If it does, the vehicle can suddenly lose the power that drives the wheels. It also means the vehicle may roll away after you shift into park, because park no longer holds it in place.

item.title: Cadillac XT5 and GMC Acadia axle shaft can separate
item.description: The right-front axle shaft that sends engine power to the wheel may not have been attached to the transmission correctly, so it can pull apart. If that happens the vehicle can suddenly lose the ability to move under its own power. Worse, with the shaft separated, shifting into park may not actually hold the vehicle, so it could roll away on its own after you get out. Dealers replace the right-front axle shaft assembly at no charge.

item.title: Buick, Cadillac, Chevy, GMC: Daytime Running Lights Stay On
item.description: On these Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet and GMC vehicles, the daytime running lights can stay lit when you turn the headlights on. They are supposed to switch off at that point. Because they stay bright, they can create glare for other drivers and make it harder for people to see. This does not meet the federal rules for vehicle lamps. A dealer can update the software that controls the lights, or the fix can be sent to the vehicle wirelessly.

item.title: Cadillac XT4 backup camera image may go blank
item.description: Certain 2019-2020 Cadillac XT4 vehicles with the optional Surround Vision feature have a video module that can lose its connection to the rearview camera. When that happens, the backup camera picture does not show up on the screen, so you cannot see what is behind the vehicle when you shift into reverse. Dealers will update the module's software, or replace the module if the update is not enough, at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and Escalade daytime running light glare
item.description: On these full-size SUVs, the daytime running lights can stay on even after you turn the headlights on. Those front lights are meant to switch off once the headlights take over. Because they don't, the front of your vehicle can shine brighter than intended and throw glare at other drivers and at you. That extra glare makes it harder to see clearly, which is why it breaks a federal lighting rule. The repair is a free software update that can be sent to the vehicle over the air.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq instrument panel can go completely blank
item.description: A software problem in the module that runs the driver's display can make the instrument panel go completely blank on some 2023 Cadillac Lyriq vehicles. That is the screen in front of you that shows how fast you are going and any warning lights. If it goes dark you lose that information while driving, which makes it easier to speed or to miss a warning about the car. GM will reload corrected software at the dealer.

item.title: Cadillac XT5, XT6 and GMC Acadia rearview camera fails
item.description: Your vehicle has the optional Surround Vision camera system. The cables that carry the backup camera's picture to your screen were crimped incorrectly when they were built. A bad crimp means the rearview camera can quit working altogether or cut in and out. When the screen goes blank you lose your view of what is directly behind the vehicle while backing up, which raises the chance of hitting something or someone. Dealers will replace the cables free.

item.title: Cadillac XT5, XT6, GMC Acadia tire label unreadable
item.description: On certain 2023 Cadillac XT5, XT6 and GMC Acadia vehicles, the sticker on the post behind the driver's door may be hard to read. That label lists the tire size your vehicle is built for, and federal rules require it to be legible. If a tire shop cannot read it, the wrong size tires could be put on the vehicle, and the wrong tires can make it harder to handle and raise crash risk.

item.title: Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and Escalade third-row seat belt flaw
item.description: This affects SUVs equipped with third-row seats. The small metal rivet that holds the seat belt buckle to its bracket may have been made wrong on the left or right third-row belt. If the rivet is not formed properly, the buckle may not hold a passenger in place during a crash, so someone in the back row could be hurt. A dealer will inspect both third-row buckles and replace them if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Cadillac XT5, XT6, GMC Acadia fuel tank valve leaks
item.description: On certain 2022 Cadillac XT5, XT6 and GMC Acadia all-wheel-drive vehicles, a valve on the fuel tank may not seal properly. That valve is meant to keep gasoline from escaping if the vehicle ever rolls over in a crash. If it is knocked out of place or missing, fuel can leak during a rollover, and spilled gasoline can catch fire. Dealers will inspect the tank and replace the tank shell if the valve is bad.

item.title: Cadillac XT5, XT6 and GMC Acadia rear suspension bolt
item.description: A bolt in the left-rear suspension may not have been tightened correctly at the factory. That bolt holds a part called the toe link, which keeps the rear wheel pointed the right way. If the bolt is loose or missing, the toe link can come apart while you are driving and the rear wheel can shift out of position. A dealer will inspect the left-rear suspension and put in a new fastener if it is loose or missing.

item.title: Cadillac XT6 brake fluid cap missing its warning label
item.description: Under the hood, the cap on the brake fluid tank is missing its printed warning label. That label is what warns against letting dirt or other debris get into the fluid when the cap is opened. Without it, the brake fluid could be contaminated without anyone realizing. Dirty brake fluid can affect how well the brakes work. Federal brake rules require the label, so these cars don't meet the standard as built.

item.title: GM vehicles may have badly welded driver seat frame
item.description: Certain Chevrolet Malibu, Equinox and Blazer models and the Cadillac XT4 may have a bad weld in the driver's seat cushion frame, in the part that tilts the seat up and down. Because the weld is not done properly, the frame may not hold the driver firmly in place during a crash. Dealers will inspect the driver's seat and replace the cushion frame if it needs it, at no charge to you. Notification letters were mailed to owners on June 23, 2022.
